capabilities: set a remote image URL as the editor background
adjust opacity, blur and contrast for legibility
exclude folders or notes from the background
disambiguation: Not a theme or CSS snippet manager; it only sets a background image from a remote URL.
extras: Only supports remote image URLs; users must host their own images. README mentions waneella animated gifs as example backgrounds.
problem: Obsidian's editor has no built-in way to display a custom background image behind note text.
summary: Appearance plugin that sets a remote image URL as the editor background, with opacity, blur, contrast and positioning controls.
